title: compact-eval-smokecheck-digest-may11-2025
body:
Compact Eval / Smokecheck digest — 2025-05-11

Overview:
Quick weekly notes from the compact eval working sync (short, team-facing). Purpose: capture the lightweight smokechecks we ran this week while onboarding 7B and 13B variants, surface any immediate regressions after 4-bit and hybrid qint runs, and list short tactical follow-ups. These are intentionally terse — this doc is a checklist + signals dump for infra, test authors, and model owners.

Attendees (sync):
- Aisha (note-taker)
- Mateo (quant infra)
- Lin (evals + metric suite)
- Jonah (model onboarding)
- Slack: #applied-ml-smokechecks thread running for async follow-ups

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Ran smokechecks against commit c3a9f2 (quant-tools) across three configurations: fp16 baseline, 4-bit symmetric (q4_sym), and 4-bit hybrid (q4_hyb).
- Primary signal: instruction-following pass-rate drop of ~1.8% absolute on q4_sym for the 13B instruction-suite; q4_hyb reduced the gap to ~0.6% versus fp16.
- Latency: median token latency improved 22% on q4_hyb on the L4 node pool; tail p95 latency unchanged within noise.
- KV-cache regen: observed 0.3% token mismatch after warm-cache replays on q4_sym at sequence length >1024; likely precision rounding in KV matmul path.
- No major safety regressions surfaced in the compact safety smoke-set (small but targeted).

Compact experiment log (short):
- Config A: fp16 baseline (model:v2.1) — 1000 inferences, instr-pass=92.4%, med-token-latency=9.8ms
- Config B: q4_sym (same model) — 1000 inferences, instr-pass=90.6%, med-token-latency=7.6ms, kv-mismatch=0.3% on long seqs
- Config C: q4_hyb (same model) — 1000 inferences, instr-pass=91.8%, med-token-latency=7.6ms, kv-mismatch~0.05%
- Small evals: 3-shot summarization BLEU-like metric delta: -0.9 (q4_sym) / -0.2 (q4_hyb) relative to fp16 on our compact metric.

Notes on methodology (cause this matters for flaky signals):
- Smokechecks are intentionally small (1k inferences) and use stratified slices: instruction-following (300), summarization (300), prompt-injection-safety (200), regression tokens (200).
- Runs executed with the same batching policy (auto-batch short) and identical KV warm-up sequences to exercise cache path.
- We use a short rolling seed sweep (3 seeds) and report median to reduce noisy runs.
- Metric thresholds: anything >1.0% instr-pass delta or >0.5% kv-mismatch flagged for triage.

Anomalies / interesting observations:
1) KV-cache mismatches are concentrated in sequences where we hit attention-sparsity micro-optimizations (example patterns attached). Suspect: accumulation order + int4 matmul rounding. Not a functional regression (outputs still sensible) but causes token-level divergence for deterministic tests.
2) One outlier failure on q4_hyb where the first token probability mass was skewed (single example). Re-ran with different seed — disappeared. Marked as flaky, likely noise in kernel scheduling.
3) Latency improvements were consistent across L4/GPU pools but p95 shows variance when model does dense recompute (related to long prompt handling).

Decisions made during sync:
- Short-term: promote q4_hyb as the default onboarding candidate for 13B family in the sandbox-canary, provided we gate on a KV-mismatch <0.2% over 5k inferences.
- Do not promote q4_sym for production canary for 13B until kv-mismatch root cause is addressed.
- Add an automated smokecheck that includes a 2-run kv-replay comparison (warm vs cold) to highlight divergence sources automatically.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Mateo: run extended kv-regression suite (50k inferences) for q4_sym and q4_hyb, collect per-layer activations for divergence analysis. Due: 2025-05-16.
- Lin: add the 2-run kv-replay step into the smokecheck pipeline PR (github.com/redwood-inference/quant-tools/pull/178). PR draft exists; finish tests by 2025-05-14.
- Jonah: update model onboarding checklist to include the instr-pass gating and kv-replay check for 13B. Due: 2025-05-15.
- Aisha: draft short runbook entry for triaging token-level mismatches (where to look: kernels, accumulation precision, layernorm drift). Due: 2025-05-18.

Open questions / research probes:
- Is the kv-mismatch due to our quantized kernel accumulation precision or a packaging difference between the fp16 and int4 runtime ramps? Probe: dump FP32 accumulation traces and compare.
- Will the observed ~1.8% instr-pass gap on q4_sym track with larger eval sets or shrink with calibration (per-channel scales)? Test plan: run 10k instr-suite with and without per-channel scale calibration.
- Can we implement a lightweight confidence-corrector layer (small FP16 adjustment) on top of int4 to fix deterministic token bias without losing latency? Quick prototype suggestion for Mateo/Jonah.

Follow-ups for infra & ops:
- Add a nightly smokecheck job (smoke-small-4k) that rotates through new model commits and posts a short digest in #applied-ml-smokechecks. Target start: 2025-05-20.
- Build a simple dashboard tile in Console (dev workspace) showing instr-pass delta, kv-mismatch, and med-token-latency per-quant-mode for recent canaries. Lin to sync with Console team.

Raw notes / adhoc captures from sync:
- "If the mismatch is only at token-level but downstream behavior unchanged, we still need to fix because deterministic evals depend on token-level equalities." — Jonah
- "q4_hyb looks promising as a default — fewer surprises so far." — Mateo
- "We should add 2 seeds to daily runs to catch flakiness early." — Lin

Attachments / quick refs:
- Short kernel sample logs and example prompts are attached in the PR: github.com/redwood-inference/quant-tools/pull/178 (see tests/kernel-dumps).
- Triage checklist placeholder: Confluence ML-SMOKE-PIPELINE -> 'kv-mismatch triage' section (draft).

If you care about specifics and want me to expand any section (long-run numbers, per-layer diffs, example prompts), ping me in thread or add to the PR review.

End of digest.
